title: Council Reaffirms Strong Statutory Protections for The Pantiles & Commons
author: Tunbridge Wells Borough Council
photo_credit: Photo: Kelly Wilcox • March for the Commons (21 March 2026)
summary: Tunbridge Wells Borough Council has issued a formal statement reaffirming its support for the Friends’ community buyout aspiration and highlighting the legal protections under the 1890 Act and Local Plan ensuring zero development rights.
body:
Tunbridge Wells Borough Council has issued a formal public statement following the commercial announcement that Targetfollow intends to sell its Tunbridge Wells estate, including The Pantiles and Tunbridge Wells and Rusthall Commons.

The Council explicitly reaffirmed its ongoing support for the Friends of Tunbridge Wells and Rusthall Commons and our aspiration to bring the Commons into charitable community ownership.

### Statutory Safeguards Under Acts of Parliament
In its statement, the Borough Council highlighted the robust legal, planning, and public access protections that safeguard the Commons:
- **1890 Improvement Act:** Governed by the statutory Tunbridge Wells Improvement Act 1890, protecting public access and prohibiting enclosure or development.
- **Adopted Local Plan:** Strict planning designations ensure zero residential or commercial development rights.
- **Statutory Conservators:** Management remains under the jurisdiction of the Commons Conservators regardless of freehold ownership.

The Council confirmed that it will look carefully at the sale of The Pantiles and work constructively with any future owner to protect heritage assets.
